A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M3GN study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation experiments on five datasets, including baseline comparisons, ablations, trajectory visualizations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds MaNGO comparisons, noisy-context and material-specific evaluations, and resource measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same CNP context encoding, aggregation, ProDMP trajectory generation, and training objective. The MaNGO adaptation and additional experimental controls do not revise the proposed M3GN procedure.

E1.justification: The five original datasets and Sheet Deformation OOD evaluation remain. V2 adds noisy-context observation scenarios on Deformable Block (Appendix E.3, Figure 19), extending evaluation to imperfect inputs. Suggested fluid applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: MaNGO, discussed but not benchmarked in v1, becomes an evaluated baseline across all five tasks. V2 also adds material-specialized MGN comparisons and includes EGNO and MaNGO in the resource comparison, substantially broadening the evaluated competitors.

E3.justification: Existing splits, training budgets, and Table 1 settings remain unchanged. New evaluations introduce context-noise levels of 0.0005, 0.001, and 0.01, and compare five separately trained material-specific MGN models with one pooled-material M3GN model. Table 3 adds memory and parameter-count measurements and separates context encoding from simulation time.

E4.justification: V2 adds two focused Deformable Block analyses in Appendix E.3 and Figure 19: sensitivity to noisy context, including a context-free control, and comparison against material-specialized MGN models. Existing movement-primitive, aggregation, history, and latent-space analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and bootstrapped confidence intervals over eight random seeds. The additional result curves use the existing reporting practice; no changed run count, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds MaNGO results throughout, including lower Falling Teddy Bear errors than M3GN at several anchor steps, plus noise/material-control findings and Table 3 resource values. Figure 9 timings are revised, and the reported maximum speedup over physics simulators changes from 400 to 700. These are additions and revisions to reported evidence, not an established same-setting improvement in M3GN.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Section 3 and the ProDMP derivations in Appendix A are unchanged, including the training likelihood and initial-condition equations. The new collider-trajectory footnote motivates an existing assumption without changing it.

C1.justification: The abstract and central algorithmic contributions remain unchanged. V2 explicitly claims to be the first study of this initial-trajectory-context setup and presents that setup as a contribution. The introduction also extends its comparative-performance claim to MaNGO.

C2.justification: V1 hypothesizes that similar falling-object context causes encoder overfitting; v2 instead suggests that later anchors increase average error by excluding easy pre-impact timesteps. V2 also interprets high-noise degradation and pooled-material performance, motivates known collider trajectories through robotic planning, and discusses possible fluid and non-mesh extensions.

D1.justification: V2 documents the MaNGO adaptation: removing its encoder, supplying context followed by repeated anchor states, and discarding context-time predictions. Table 3 newly provides model parameter counts and a runtime breakdown. Existing hardware, hyperparameter, preprocessing, and code-access disclosures remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds explicit first-study positioning for the experimental setup and removes the manufacturing-observation example and its Zeeb et al. (2025) citation. MaNGO was already cited and discussed in v1; the related-work section otherwise remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction is locally reordered to foreground context-based meta-learning. V2 adds explanatory passages and a footnote, reorganizes Appendix E into additional subsections, and adds publication and review information. Most prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: Existing plot designs gain MaNGO curves and legends, and six rollout grids gain a MaNGO row. V2 adds Figure 19 and Table 3, clarifies color labels, corrects Figure 6's log-scale caption wording, and relocates several figures. These extend the existing presentation without a broad redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the empirical assessment through MaNGO comparisons, targeted noise/material controls, and explicit resource accounting. Reporting competitor wins and high-noise degradation makes the evidence more informative. The gains remain focused: the new ablations cover Deformable Block only and leave details such as noise generation and the exact five material settings unspecified.
